text:
Maya: Heads up - saw a telemetry snapshot flood from OOB agents in us-west1 GPU racks at ~08:12 UTC, causing the provisioner to backpressure. Some nodes toggled secure boot to 'enabled' during the last firmware push. Anyone oncall?
Alex: @Maya that's the canary group, saw increased BMC log churn too. Provisioner queue length spiked to 42 and allocation stalled. Key log snippet: `oob: snapshot_size=3.2MB rate=120/s error=queue_overrun`
infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: oob-telemetry-snapshot-throttle triggered for rack-gpu-12 (us-west1). Automatic rate-limit applied.
Sasha: Repro note: when the telemetry stream floods the ingest broker, the GPU allocator stalls waiting for serial health-check IVs. That blocks new pods.
Maya: I'm grabbing the runbook (telemetry-flood v2). Immediate plan: 1) mute telemetry for affected rack, 2) graceful drain, 3) manual rollback of BIOS/fw if required.
Alex: Quick check I ran on one host:
```
ssh jump@oob-gpu-12
sudo systemctl stop oob-telemetry.service
journalctl -u oob-telemetry -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 50
cat /var/log/bmc/last-commit.log | tail -n 80
```
Sasha: Don't use `tcp_tw_recycle` in prod (breaks NAT). If TCP backlog is the issue, bump `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=4096` and tune the broker ingest concurrency instead.
Ryan: Are the secure-boot flag flips correlated with the fw rollout? We observed 6 nodes flip to enabled and then hang in provisioning.
Maya: Cross-checking the batch: all 6 hit BIOS 2.1.8 during the midnight push from staging->canary. Previous was 2.1.7. BMC reboot stacks show `commit_handler: set_secure_boot=1` right after apply. Suspect firmware regression.
Tobi: oncall-Tobi here — starting rollback to 2.1.7 for rack-gpu-12 now. ETA ~12m. Also disabling live telemetry streaming for the canary pool to stop the ingest pressure.
Alex: FYI cost impact: allocator stall delayed spot evictions and preemptions; roughly ~3h of delayed jobs across customers -> ballpark $2.1k in spot/throughput penalties. Logging a ticket for billing.
Sasha: Adding temporary routing: send telemetry from canary -> cold storage S3 (batched) instead of live pipeline until we root-cause. Should cut ingest rate by ~90%.
Maya: After rollback I'll trigger controlled repro on a single node (non-prod tag) to confirm stable boot and no secure-boot flip. If repro fails we'll open an emergency vendor escalation for 2.1.8.
infra-bot: Update: rollback started for rack-gpu-12 by Tobi at 08:36 UTC. status=rolling progress=3/6 hosts done
Ryan: Good catch. If you see nodes stuck in `secureboot=enabled, provision_state=awaiting-kick` ping me directly and I'll jump to force-provision.
Maya: Created incident INC-2024-4558, linked the telemetry-flood runbook and the rollback play. Will follow up with a short postmortem once stable.
Alex: :thumbsup:
